kill_fact: No clean kill of the SoP base: the ex-Brazil Employee Benefits franchise (+9.4% organic, 37.0% recurring EBITDA margin, EUR210m H1 recurring FCF at 86% conversion) and a real ~EUR1.27bn net-financial-cash floor (EXCLUDING the separately-reported EUR753m restricted float) all verify against the primary H1 FY26 release, and even a fully-binding Brazil case lands the bear SoP (~EUR14.9-17.5) at/above the ~EUR11.43 price. The thesis survives attack but required correcting three load-bearing claims (below), and the moat is NARROW + ERODING by regulation, which caps value conviction.
corrections: (1) NET-CASH ANCHOR OVERSTATED IN BOTH CASES. The debate/bull repeatedly cite '~EUR2.0bn net cash (cash 3.31B vs debt 1.29B)' as unpriced optionality; the bear claims 'excess cash FELL EUR140m in H1.' BOTH are wrong vs primary: the official H1 FY26 release reports net financial cash EXCLUDING restricted cash of EUR1,270m at 28-Feb-2026, UP +EUR107m from EUR1,163m at 31-Aug-2025 (gross debt EUR1,271m; restricted float EUR753m reported separately; float-related cash EUR2,855m also ROSE +EUR119m). The EUR2.0bn headline conflates net cash with voucher float and must be retired; true distributable floor is ~EUR1.27bn. This cuts the bull's net-cash overlay hard and also voids the bear's 'float is shrinking' optic (float grew). (2) BRAZIL HEDGE IS DEAD / MAGNITUDE WORSE. The 27-Jan-2026 injunction that suspended PAT penalties was OVERTURNED on 24-Feb-2026 (judge sided with the government; companies must comply immediately; no merits ruling expected before end-2026), so 'the worst case may not fully bind' is false — full implementation (3.6% merchant-commission cap, 15-day settlement, ~360-day interoperability) is the base case. Management framing implies ~40% Brazil revenue loss in H2 FY26 rising to 50-60% by early FY27 — if anything DEEPER than the bear's '~50%'. The bear's structural (not cyclical) framing is CONFIRMED and more binding. (3) CHILE CLAIM MISCHARACTERIZED. The 27-May-2026 Chilean Competition Authority (FNE/TDLC) claim is NOT a new payments-disintermediation/take-rate front as the dossier/valley_of_death implies — it is a backward-looking cartel/collusion case (alleged market-sharing 2013-2021) seeking a ~USD39.6m fine against Pluxee Chile, with leniency granted to the reporting competitor. Small historical antitrust fine, not a forward unit-economics threat. (4) Buyback verifies EXACTLY: 8,347,225 shares repurchased 31-Oct-2025 to 8-May-2026 at avg EUR11.98 (above spot); 5,843,058 shares (3.97% of capital) to be cancelled. The capital-allocation 'put' is real but spent/FIRED. (5) Bear's 'interchange capped at 2%' sub-figure is not corroborated by primary releases (they cite the 3.6% MDR cap + 15-day settlement + interoperability); not load-bearing, flagged unverified. Discount is shared sector-regulatory beta not idiosyncratic alpha (Pluxee de-rated on the same PAT/Italy shock as Edenred; fwd consensus EPS ~+0.6%; net retention rolled to ~100%).
evidence: Pluxee, 'First Half Fiscal 2026 Results', 16-Apr-2026 (GlobeNewswire / pluxeegroup.com): net financial cash EXCLUDING restricted cash EUR1,270m at 28-Feb-2026 vs EUR1,163m at 31-Aug-2025 (+EUR107m); gross debt EUR1,271m; float-related cash EUR2,855m (EUR753m restricted); revenue EUR655m +5.6% organic, recurring EBITDA EUR242m at 37.0% margin (+229bps), recurring FCF EUR210m / 86% conversion; FY26 guide cut to stable organic revenue + slight margin expansion (vs prior high-single-digit / +100bps); Brazil impact extends into H1 FY27, return to profitable growth from H2 FY27.

Reuters via Investing.com, 'Brazil judge overrules decisions suspending changes to meal voucher system', 24-Feb-2026: judge sided with the government, overturning the prior injunctions for Pluxee and Edenred's Ticket; companies must resume complying with the new PAT rules immediately; Pluxee does not expect a merits decision before end-2026. PAT decree (signed Nov-2025): 3.6% merchant-commission/MDR cap, settlement cut 30->15 days, interoperability among meal/food benefit issuers mandated within ~1 year; Brazil ~29% of group revenue.

Pluxee, 'completion of a 100 million euros share buyback program', 11-May-2026 (GlobeNewswire): 8,347,225 shares repurchased 31-Oct-2025 to 8-May-2026 at avg EUR11.98; 5,843,058 shares (3.97% of ordinary capital) resolved to be cancelled.

Pluxee, 'acknowledges the filing of a claim by the Chilean Competition Authority', 27-May-2026 (GlobeNewswire) + Concurrences/Reuters: FNE/TDLC claim re alleged collusion 2013-2021 in the benefit-voucher sector, ~USD39.6m fine sought against Pluxee Chile, leniency granted to the reporting competitor — historical antitrust, not a forward take-rate reform.
